title: onboard apply resolves templates from the invocation root, never current_exe
action: Backlog debt row 659: onboard apply resolves its template source via current_exe(), so in a granted worktree whose .bee/bin/bee is a symlink into MAIN, /proc/self/exe resolves to MAIN's checkout and apply splices MAIN's AGENTS.block.md content over the worktree's AGENTS.md — silently overwriting worktree edits. Fix: locate the current_exe()-based source resolution in the onboard module (declared file apply.rs is a guess — follow the real site) and replace it: the template/source root is derived from the PROJECT ROOT of the invocation (the repo root onboard is already given or resolves from cwd), so a worktree renders from its own checkout's templates. When that root carries no templates (a host repo without bee source), refuse with a typed error naming the invocation root and the missing path — never silently fall back to the exe's checkout. TDD red-first: fixture with two checkouts (a fake MAIN with distinctive template bytes and a fake worktree with different bytes, exe-equivalent resolution pointed at MAIN) proving apply renders the WORKTREE's bytes; a no-templates root refuses naming both paths; existing onboard tests stay green.

truths: a worktree onboard apply renders its own checkout's templates, never the exe's checkout
a root without templates refuses naming both paths
existing onboard behavior for the ordinary single-checkout case is byte-identical

artifacts.substantive: root-derived source resolution plus tests, no TODO stubs (or the real site, named in the trace)

trace.outcome: Engine::locate walks up from current_dir only (never current_exe); typed LocateError names invocation root + missing template; refusal payload carries both; real site source.rs not apply.rs, noted per instruction
